h1: Tints of Blue Hotel — Rooftop Saltwater Pool and Free Breakfast on Sukhumvit Soi 27
intro: For the price of a decent 3-star, Tints of Blue Hotel quietly overdelivers: a rooftop saltwater pool on the 8th floor with Bangkok skyline views, a free breakfast that guests consistently rave about, a complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle to BTS Asok, and 42 individually decorated rooms spread across 7 design themes — all on a calm residential soi just one BTS stop from Phrom Phong's EM District. Scored 9.0/10 from 5,638 Agoda reviews and 9.3/10 from over 1,400 Booking.com reviews. From approx. ฿1,500/night including breakfast.

body.html: Sukhumvit Soi 27 runs on the odd-numbered side of the main road — quieter than the busier even-numbered sois across the way, but just a short hop to everything. Tints of Blue Hotel originally opened in 2015 and underwent a full renovation in 2022, emerging with a design identity built around natural materials: rattan, warm wood, and cascading greenery that make it feel more like a thoughtfully restored townhouse than a generic chain property. Each of the 42 rooms follows one of 7 distinct design themes, which means no two rooms look quite the same.

The detail that shows up in almost every review is the rooftop saltwater pool on the 8th floor, open around the clock. In the evening, the Bangkok skyline lights up behind you while you float in warm water — a genuinely special experience for a hotel at this price point. The fitness centre sits adjacent to the pool. For a 3-star property to offer a private rooftop pool in the Sukhumvit corridor is unusual, and guests clearly notice.
"Woke up to a genuinely good breakfast — fresh eggs, good coffee — then went up to the rooftop pool with the skyline view. Hard to believe this cost less than many standard rooms nearby."

The free breakfast buffet is served daily from 7:30 AM in the 2nd-floor restaurant. Real guest sentiment here is consistently strong: fresh-squeezed juice, made-to-order eggs, a rotating selection of Thai and Western options, and quality coffee. Breakfast is included in the room rate, not bolted on as an optional add-on, which makes the base price feel even better value. The café and bar on the same floor stay open through the day.

Location sits on Sukhumvit Soi 27 — BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit are approximately 700 m away. That is a 10-minute walk in Bangkok heat or rain, which is why the hotel runs a complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle to the main road and BTS Asok from 7 AM to 10 PM. From Asok it is one stop to BTS Phrom Phong where Emporium, EmQuartier and EmSphere all cluster together; Terminal 21 is right at Asok. The hotel also offers bicycle rentals for guests who prefer to explore independently.

Rooms come with a small kitchenette, refrigerator, in-room safe, and flat-screen TV. Several room types include a private balcony. Trip.com guests score service at 9.7/10 and cleanliness at 9.4/10. The one honest caution from real reviews: soundproofing in certain rooms is not perfect — some guests noted they could hear neighbours through the walls. If you are a light sleeper, mention it at check-in and ask for a quieter room; the soi itself is quiet, so internal noise is the main variable.

Tints of Blue consistently earns its high scores across all platforms — 9.0 on Agoda (5,638 reviews), 9.3 on Booking.com (1,421+ reviews), 9.4 on Trip.com (125 reviews), and a 4.6/5 TripAdvisor bubble rating from 621 reviews, ranking it #14 among Bangkok B&Bs and boutique inns. It is the kind of place that converts one-time guests into repeat visitors — people come back specifically for the breakfast, the rooftop, and the staff. For budget-conscious travellers who want boutique charm without boutique prices, this is hard to beat in this part of Sukhumvit.

honestSummary: Tints of Blue Hotel clearly punches above its 3-star classification. The combination of a rooftop pool, included breakfast, free tuk-tuk service, and genuinely warm staff in a boutique setting from around ฿1,500/night makes it one of the strongest value propositions in this part of Sukhumvit. The main trade-off is a 10-minute walk (or short tuk-tuk ride) to BTS rather than a doorstep station.
honestChecks: If you need to catch the BTS before 7 AM daily — the tuk-tuk shuttle starts at 7 AM; before that you will walk or take a motorbike taxi. If early departures are frequent, ibis Sukhumvit 24 (100 m from BTS) may suit you better.
If you are a light sleeper who is sensitive to noise — mention it at check-in and request a room with better soundproofing. The street outside is quiet; the variable is walls between rooms.
If you need a pool for serious lap swimming — the rooftop pool is compact and best suited for relaxing. For lane swimming, look at properties with larger pools in the area.

tips.title: Use the Free Tuk-Tuk — It Actually Works
tips.body: The hotel runs a free tuk-tuk to BTS Asok and the main road, 7 AM–10 PM. Tell the front desk 5 minutes before you need it. This solves the only real inconvenience of the location.

tips.title: Rooftop at Dusk Is the Best Time
tips.body: The 8th-floor pool looks best when the Bangkok skyline lights up in the evening. It is rarely crowded — grab a spot, order a drink from the bar, and stay for the view.

tips.title: Order Your Eggs at the Breakfast Counter
tips.body: Buffet breakfast runs 7:30–11 AM. The made-to-order eggs (omelette, scrambled, fried) are a highlight — just tell the staff your preference. Coffee is proper filter coffee, not instant.

tips.title: EM District Is One BTS Stop Away
tips.body: Tuk-tuk to BTS Asok, one stop on the BTS to Phrom Phong — Emporium, EmQuartier and EmSphere are all right there. Door to shopping in under 20 minutes total.

faqTitle: FAQ — Tints of Blue Hotel Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Tints of Blue Hotel and how do I get there?
faq.a: The hotel is at 47 Sukhumvit Soi 27, Watthana, Bangkok 10110. BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit are approximately 700 m away — about a 10-minute walk. The hotel provides a free tuk-tuk shuttle to BTS Asok from 7 AM to 10 PM, so you rarely need to walk in the heat.

faq.q: Is breakfast really free at Tints of Blue Hotel?
faq.a: Yes — buffet breakfast is included in every room rate, served 7:30–11:00 AM on the 2nd floor. The spread includes made-to-order eggs, good coffee, fresh fruit, Thai dishes and Western options. It is consistently praised as one of the best free breakfasts guests have encountered in Bangkok.

faq.q: What is the rooftop pool like at Tints of Blue Hotel?
faq.a: The rooftop saltwater pool is on the 8th floor with city skyline views. It is open 24 hours a day. The pool is compact — ideal for relaxing and floating rather than serious lap swimming — but the views and the 24-hour access make it a genuine highlight. The fitness centre is directly beside it.

faq.q: How much does Tints of Blue Hotel cost per night?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿1,500/night for a Studio Room (including free breakfast). Studio Suites run around ฿1,800, Premier Studios around ฿2,200, and Family Rooms around ฿2,800. All rates include the breakfast buffet. Prices vary by season and platform — compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com for the best deal.

faq.q: Is Tints of Blue Hotel close to the Emporium and EM District?
faq.a: One BTS stop away. Take the free tuk-tuk to BTS Asok, ride one stop to BTS Phrom Phong, and you are at Emporium, EmQuartier and EmSphere. Total journey is typically 15–20 minutes door to mall. Terminal 21 is right at BTS Asok and can be reached even faster.
